values: Materials and timing｜45 minutes, entirely fictional

5 minutes to read the rules, 15 minutes to fill in the three-position table, 10 minutes for handover, 10 minutes to score and correct errors, 5 minutes to reconcile. All three paper counter samples P1/P2/P3 record the service as S; the fictional price is 6 yuan each, with a receipt Q1/Q2/Q3 for 6 yuan received. Only the service, amount and receipt are checked here; an unclear destination remains pending verification, and this cannot be used to conclude that real acceptance is complete.

P1 label 2002→target B2; R1 stop 2 requires a signature but the recipient is absent; the P2 label code is unreadable and there is no route stop order; P3 label 1001→target B1, and R1 stop 1 requires no signature and in this exercise the address has been verified and the item has been handed to the designated place.

The task compares positions using the paper materials provided and does not simulate the full lifecycle of real mail. The location pending verification is X1 and the handover time is T0; the fictional counter supervisor checks the transaction, the processing supervisor checks the P2 label and the route supervisor checks the undelivered P1. All codes, addresses, amounts and records are fictional, with no real equipment or real customer data used.
Deliverables and fields

A three-row table: for each item list the item number; counter service, amount due, amount received and receipt; the paper sorting target or pending status; the route stop order; signature conditions and physical facts; the final paper status; the basis and the next responsible person. A target container does not mean the machine has actually processed it, and counter verification does not replace real acceptance admission.

The two exception handovers list the item number, known facts, current status and storage location, unmet conditions, T0 and the next responsible person; do not guess a code for P2, and do not sign on behalf of P1 or falsely record delivery.
Complete reference answer

All three counter samples are S, with 6 due and 6 received, and Q1/Q2/Q3 each correspond to their own item numbers; only the paper fields agree, and this cannot confirm that real acceptance is complete. P1 has sorting target B2, and R1 stop 2 requires a signature but no one is present, so the attempt is undelivered and referred to the route supervisor; P2 is pending sorting verification at X1 with no usable stop order, does not enter the route and is referred to the processing supervisor; P3 has sorting target B1, and R1 stop 1 requires no signature with the address and actual delivery facts given, so this exercise records it as delivered.

Route order: P3 stop 1 then P1 stop 2; P2 does not go on the route. Targets: one item for B1, one for B2 and one pending verification, 3 in total, all paper target counts rather than actual machine throughput; the final state is 1 delivered, 1 attempted but undelivered and 1 pending sorting verification, 3 in total. T0 handover of P1: the person who must sign is absent and the undelivered item is retained and referred to the route supervisor; P2: the code is unreadable, X1 is pending verification and there is no route eligibility, so it is referred to the processing supervisor; do not fabricate notification methods or return procedures.
Scoring, error samples and feedback

Four dimensions scored 0–2 each, 8 in total: reconciliation of the three counter item fields, routing and route status, exception handover, and data and authority. 2 points is complete and correct, 1 point is the right direction but with missing fields or explanations, and 0 points is a mismatched amount, guessed code, false status, inability to hand over, use of real data or exceeding authority.

Error sample: the counter is correct and entirely fictional, but P1 falsely records delivery, P2 guesses B1 and puts it on the route, and there is no exception handover: 2/0/0/2=4/8. Feedback: keep the correct counter fields for all three mail items, restore P1 as attempted but undelivered and P2 as X1, and add the two T0 handovers and next responsible persons; check sorting 1+1+1=3 and the final 1+1+1=3. The score is learning feedback for this task only, not a hiring examination. Real rates, acceptance, signatures, returns, equipment and driving follow institutional training and authorization.

subject.name: Postal Service Workers
subject.summary: Postal service workers are the BLS 43-5050 summary occupational group, covering postal counter clerks, mail carriers and mail sorters, processors and machine operators. Counter acceptance and charging, centre routing and route delivery each have different work objects, environments and authority. When job hunting, choose a specific position first, then check the announcement, training, wages and shifts; the overall figures on this page cannot be treated as any single breakout or as individual treatment.
